note: Where the shop is. Cyberpunk RED prints no shops, only the atlas's places and what each one is, so which of them will sell you something, and what kind of seller they are, is a house rule read off the blurbs. A shop is a PLACE you travel to: it sells the way one of the four archetypes in engine/vendors.ts does (street, gun_shop, armorer; the fixer is a person and is reached by phone from anywhere) and carries its own name and line. Nothing here may invent a fact the atlas contradicts; the line says what the blurb already says. Every place must exist in the atlas and be tagged as somewhere things are sold, and a test holds both. Prices, stock and owners are the next layer and are not here yet.
visitNote: What a visit costs once you are standing at the counter: the trip there is the atlas's own and is paid when you travel, so the archetype's 'there and back' time is not charged a second time. The fixer is a call and keeps its own wait.

shops.label: Ganymede Street Market
shops.line: Stalls along the street the map is named for, open at every hour the Tyger Claws allow it.

shops.label: Dock 13
shops.line: Willy Maze's storefront, and on the right nights his night market, under the dock lights.

shops.label: Woodchipper's Garage
shops.line: Tailgates down in Woodchipper's yard, engines ticking, on the nights she opens it.

shops.label: Mrs. Suzuki's Bodega
shops.line: The most stable shelves in Old Japantown, and the only stock you can count on.

shops.label: Bits'n'Bolts
shops.line: A hole-in-the-wall tech shop where every drawer is half something else.

shops.label: Bits’n’Bolts: Faisal’s drawer
shops.line: Faisal’s weapons, sold through the tech shop’s back counter. Ask for what is in the drawer, not what is on the shelf.

shops.label: Minimallism
shops.line: Tables set up in the husk of an old mall, on the side nobody's reclaimed yet.

shops.label: The Swap
shops.line: Parts on tables, and provenance is not a question anybody working them considers polite.

shops.label: The Armory: the gun cage
shops.line: 6th Street's headquarters, behind the old National Guard walls. They sell, and they watch you do it.

shops.label: The Armory: the plate racks
shops.line: Racks of plate in a drill hall that was built to hold exactly this.

shops.label: Toggle's Temple
shops.line: A counter beside the firing lanes, run by a man with strong opinions about who is watching.

shops.label: Skiv's Counter
shops.line: A dockside bar with an office at the back. Both halves of the business are open to anyone.

shops.label: Torrell and Chiang's
shops.line: The best tailors in Night City, who know that good tailoring and good armor are the same job.

shops.label: Oasis Megamart
shops.line: Aisle after aisle under Continental Brands’ roof, with the ammunition in sporting goods, somewhere past the pet food.

shops.label: Executive Zone Oasis
shops.line: Premium brands and rarities, fresh-cut flowers by drone, and an attendant who knows your address before you do.

shops.label: Canalside Plaza
shops.line: A strip mall with a talent agency, a restaurant and a nail salon, and one unit at the end with the lights off at the front and on at the back.

shops.label: Ruggels Way Surplus
shops.line: Flares, dry bags and crates that fell off boats. Hollis Ruggels has a story for every one, and none of them match.

shops.label: Dragon’s Tooth Pawn
shops.line: Watches and jade in the window. The back shelf holds whatever the Red Chrome Legion pledged against a bad week.

shops.label: The Co-Op
shops.line: Engineering students selling ex-lab kit and the contents of a Biotechnica skip, and haggling like they are defending a thesis.

shops.label: Gentry & Blake
shops.line: A showroom for security details: heavy catalogues, serious prices, and a salesman who measures you twice and does not say why.

shops.label: The Slammer Dock Door
shops.line: A folding table in a loading dock, guns by the box. Scythe Security patrols out front and has never once turned its head.

shops.label: The Quartermaster
shops.line: Edgerunners Inc’s supply cage. Dot behind the grille grades customers on a scale that has nothing to do with money.

shops.label: Gate Surplus
shops.line: Vests with last year’s issue numbers, boots, and crates of mixed ammunition nobody has counted, under a tarp outside the wire.

shops.label: Hachiman Arms
shops.line: Receipted, regulated and politely suspicious. Mr. Hachiman files everything in triplicate, including your face.

shops.label: Ascent Outfitters
shops.line: Armour-lined coats for people who want to look like they are climbing, and survive the fall. The fitting room window looks onto the Exec Zone wall.

shops.label: The Tool Crib
shops.line: The day shift draws kit and the night shift signs it back in. Whatever is not signed back in is for sale at a fair price.
